assessment:
The table assumes the tutor in this deck is a card they can kill. It is your commander, it costs you no card at all, and it never runs out — and there is exactly one entry below because there is no second searcher anywhere in the 99. This section is the whole wish list.

Read the gate, not the mana. Her activation puts a legendary permanent with mana value strictly less than her power onto the battlefield, and her power is bought with colours among your OTHER legends. One colour opens ten targets, two opens twenty-three, three opens twenty-eight and four opens all thirty-three — so spend the whole early game buying that second colour, because it is thirteen cards of access on a single drop. Then stop climbing. Nothing here costs more than five, so the fifth colour is stats you did not need.

Budget one activation per turn cycle and pick the fetch accordingly. Set the pivot at turn five or six and stop expecting two: your mean available mana on turn six is 5.869 against a bill of five coloured pips with zero generic, and the source that pays that bill lands by turn six in only 55.8% of games. Whether a legend you just fetched can help pay for the next activation in the same turn did not clear the checker here — so treat a chain as a gift when it happens and never build a turn on it.

Now the discipline that separates good Sisay pilots from the rest. Twenty-six of the 99 are non-legendary and outside her reach at any power: every counterspell, both free protection instants, three of the six things that can pay her bill. Fetch only what she alone can reach. Draw the rest, and stop wishing for cards she was never going to find.

targets.scenario: The default. Turn 4-5, two colours among your other legends — Katilda's green and white, say — so Sisay is a 4/4 and the gate reads 'cheaper than four'. You can pay the five pips once and nobody is pressuring you.
targets.why: Buy the next wish with this wish. Derevi costs three and brings white, blue and green on one card, so a single fetch walks the ladder toward the twenty-eight and thirty-three rungs. She reads as a fair 2/3 that taps or untaps a permanent when your creatures connect, and she is the checker-verified half of your kill (stack 002). Take access today and the loop's quiet half for later, on a card nobody answers.

targets.scenario: The fuel fetch. Three colours up, Sisay a 5/5, but you are paying the activation off lands alone and a second one this rotation is out of reach.
targets.why: Fetch the battery, because half of it is invisible to you — Bloom Tender, Faeburrow Elder and Relic of Legends are all non-legendary, and Selvala is the piece Sisay can actually go and get. Her {G} and a tap make X mana in any combination of colours, X being your largest creature's power, so at Sisay 5 that is the entire bill in one activation. Her ability taps, so she wakes up next turn: fetch her the turn before you need the second activation, not the turn you need it.

targets.scenario: The answer fetch, under pressure. Three colours up, Sisay a 5/5, and the pod has already shown you the shrink attack — a colour rung eating spot removal in response to an activation.
targets.why: Retire the attack that actually beats you. She costs four, so she is legal the moment the gate reads 'cheaper than five', and she hands you, your planeswalkers and every other creature hexproof — every future colour rung becomes untargetable. She does not protect herself, so go and get her before you need her rather than after. Sweepers and -X/-X still get through, so keep a two-colour legend in hand as the rebuild.

targets.scenario: The lock-breaker. A stax seat has an artifact or enchantment squeezing your five-pip, zero-generic activation, and the frame is blunt about your role: you are the beatdown, racing the lock's completion.
targets.why: Go and get the only answer she can see. Loran is the deck's one artifact-or-enchantment removal stapled to a legendary body, live from two colours at three mana, and her enter trigger should destroy the piece locking YOU rather than the scariest piece on the table. Then tap her to draw yourself and one opponent a card, and pick the opponent whose help you want next turn.

targets.scenario: The one nobody sees coming. The combo seat is one untap from trying it, and your counterspells are exactly where they always are — in the blind spot, not your hand.
targets.why: Fetch a planeswalker out of a battlefield tutor and watch the table recalculate. He is legal from two colours at three mana, and holding opponents to sorcery speed deletes instant-speed combo and instant-speed interaction in one line — the closest thing to tutorable disruption you own, since all six counterspells must be drawn. Keep the minus-three in your pocket as the answer for a problem already on the battlefield.

targets.scenario: The closing fetch. Derevi is on the battlefield with another attacker beside her, and you can produce {W}{U}{B}{R}{G} twice this turn — once for the fetch, once held for combat.
targets.why: Take her on the turn she wins and not one turn earlier. Stack 002 is your script: five untapped lands pre-fund combat 1, combat 2 breaks even on Derevi's untaps, and the first defending player dies during combat 4 — at zero life paid, because Command Tower and Plaza of Heroes cover all five colours and City of Brass never has to tap. Until that turn she is worth more in the library, where a bracket 4 table cannot read her off your mana base and you can go and get her at will.

tutors.notes: Never activate into a cold board. At power 2 the gate is 'cheaper than two' and it is nearly empty — Mox Amber adds no colour, and a Mikaeus put onto the battlefield was never cast, which leaves what he arrives as an open question here rather than a plan. Land a colour-diverse legend first and fire next turn instead. And know your second choice before you announce the first: the power check happens on resolution, so the fetch you name is not always the fetch you get.

gaps: The blind spot is structural, so build around it rather than resenting it: twenty-six of the 99 are non-legendary and unreachable at any power — all six counterspells, both free protection instants, all four Game Changers, and three of the six things that can pay her bill. She finds payoffs; you draw fuel and stack-speed protection. Two open questions sit under the wish list and neither has cleared a checker here — whether a fetched Mikaeus arrives as anything, and whether a freshly fetched legend can help pay for a second activation the same turn. Plan on one activation per turn cycle, take protection into the 79.8% the sim has available by turn six rather than sandbagging for it, and let a chain be a gift when the game hands you one.
